cases.description: Normal case – the evaluation path contains several elements ['root','child','leaf']; toString() should return the last element 'leaf' (getName(-1)).
Single‑element path – when the evaluation path consists of a single name ['only'], getName(-1) returns that name, so toString() should return 'only'.
Empty path – a JsonNodePath that holds no names returns null (or an empty string) for getName(-1). The test verifies that toString() propagates this null result.
Null evaluation path – if getEvaluationPath() returns null, toString() will throw a NullPointerException. The test asserts that this exception is thrown.
Path implementation throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for getName(-1) when the internal list is empty. The test confirms that toString() does not swallow the exception and propagates it.

group: BaseJsonValidator.toString – special characters in last path element

cases.description: The evaluation path contains several elements and the last element includes a variety of special characters. toString() should return the exact last element without alteration.
The evaluation path ends with a name that consists solely of spaces. toString() must return those spaces unchanged, proving it does not trim the result.

group: BaseJsonValidator.toString – mixed null and valid elements

cases.description: The evaluation path contains a null element before the final one (e.g., ["root", null, "finalNode"]). toString() should ignore the null earlier element and return the last valid name.
A subclass of JsonNodePath is injected that deliberately throws IllegalStateException when getName(-1) is called. toString() must propagate this unchecked exception unchanged.

group: BaseJsonValidator.toString – evaluation path returns empty string

cases.description: The evaluation path’s last element is an empty string (e.g., ["root", ""]). toString() should return the empty string exactly, confirming that null and empty string are distinguished.
A subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides getEvaluationPath() to throw IllegalStateException. The toString() method should propagate this unchecked exception unchanged.
A subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides getEvaluationPath() to throw a generic RuntimeException. The test verifies that toString() does not catch the exception and it propagates.
A custom JsonNodePath implementation is returned by getEvaluationPath() where getName(-1) deliberately throws UnsupportedOperationException. The toString() method should propagate this exception.

A custom JsonNodePath implementation is returned by getEvaluationPath() where getName(-1) validates the index and throws IllegalArgumentException for negative values. The test ensures toString() propagates the exception.
